name: Waimakariri Biodiversity Contestable Fund - Community Organisations
summary: Annual council funding for community groups in the Waimakariri District working to protect, maintain and enhance biodiversity, usable for operational costs such as wages and overheads or for capital items such as equipment.
reporting: A report on how the funds were used is required at the end of the 12-month funding period.

eligibility.rule: Is a legal entity, such as an incorporated society or charitable trust
Vision and projects align with the Strategy and its Implementation Plan actions
Capital projects align with Implementation Plan actions
For operational funding, can engage communities and advise district landowners
No legally required, completed, beautification or primarily profit-driven work

status.quote: Applications open from 1 February to 15 March 2026.

opens.quote: Applications open from 1 February to 15 March 2026.

deadline.quote: Applications open from 1 February to 15 March 2026.

applicant_types.quote: The fund is only open to community groups working in the Waimakariri District to implement goals outlined in the Waimakariri Natural Environment Strategy.

geography.quote: The fund is only open to community groups working in the Waimakariri District to implement goals outlined in the Waimakariri Natural Environment Strategy.

access.quote: Applications from community organisations can be made by sending a completed copy of the Biodiversity Contestable Fund Application Form to

window.quote: Funding rounds will be opened annually and allocated for a 12-month period.

pool.quote: There is $10,000 (excluding GST) available for allocation to successful applicants each year

reporting.quote: A report detailing the use of the funds will be required at the end of the funding period.

effort.quote: Applications open from 1 February to 15 March 2026.

eligibility.quote: The community organisation must be a legal entity, such as an incorporated society or charitable trust.

The organisational vision and proposed projects must align with the Waimakariri Natural Environment Strategy and be specifically linked to actions outlined in the Waimakariri Natural Environment Strategy Implementation Plan.
Where capital funding is sought, projects must align with actions set out in the Implementation Plan.

Where operational funding is sought, the community organisation must be able to provide community engagement support and education/advice to Waimakariri District landowners for indigenous biodiversity projects.

For work that there is a legal obligation to do; (ii) To compensate for work already done. It is intended to assist with the cost of future work; and (iii) For beautification projects, or to support those driven primarily for financial gain.

after_award.quote: A report detailing the use of the funds will be required at the end of the funding period.
